one_liner: Neighbourhood coffee and matcha shops with app ordering and rewards
audience: urban 18-34s in New York, LA and London: students, creatives, finance and agency workers who buy a drink on the walk to work or between classes, plus matcha-obsessed girls who post their cup (inferred)
core_pain: the daily coffee run is either overpriced and slow, or cheap and tastes bad, and the matcha at most places is dusty, bitter and served in a boring cup
old_way_objects: a 20 minute queue at the third wave place
cold brew in a carton from the corner store
scenes: 8:40am on a Manhattan sidewalk, someone power-walking to the office holding a paper cup, already texting that they're five minutes away
a student in a Williamsburg flat whisking clumpy matcha in a mug with a fork, giving up and putting on shoes
two friends meeting on Prince Street, one holding the door with a drink in each hand, deciding which seasonal flavour to get before it's gone
proof_points: first store launched August 2020 as a coffee cart in the garden of the Wythe Diner in Williamsburg
over 100 shops across the US and UK
Autumn specials: Cinnamon Bun Matcha, Cinnamon Bun Latte, Harvest Chai Matcha, Harvest Chai Latte
retail range includes matcha tin, lighter roast, darker roast and The Sleeve
app ordering, Rewards programme and an Insiders programme
The Sleeve listed as sold out
do_not_say: health, energy or wellness claims about matcha or caffeine (no 'boosts metabolism', 'calms anxiety', 'better than coffee for you')
naming or comparing to Starbucks, Dunkin, Blue Bottle or any other chain
'cheapest coffee' or price promises the site does not state
invented store counts, wait times, sales figures or customer numbers
'organic', 'ceremonial grade' or sourcing claims not stated on the site
marketing-speak like 'revolutionary', 'game-changing', 'the best coffee in the world'
cta: order ahead in the app, join Rewards, or find your nearest store
